---
title: API cache reference
description: Every method on c.get("cache") in VitNode API routes - signatures, return values, TTLs, key prefixes, serialization and behavior without Redis.
icon: List
---

`c.get("cache")` is available in every Hono route handler. It stores JSON values in Redis under a per-plugin prefix, and falls back to a small in-memory store when Redis is not configured. For a step-by-step example, see [Cache API data](/docs/dev/cache/api).

## Methods

| Method                                 | Returns                                                | Behavior                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get<T>(key)`                          | `Promise<T \| null>`                                   | Reads and parses a value. Returns `null` on a miss or on a Redis error.                                                                        |
| `set<T>(key, value, ttlSeconds?)`      | `Promise<void>`                                        | Stores `value` as JSON. Without `ttlSeconds`, or with `0`, the key never expires.                                                              |
| `has(key)`                             | `Promise<boolean>`                                     | Whether the key exists. `false` on a Redis error.                                                                                              |
| `remember<T>(key, ttlSeconds, loader)` | `Promise<T>`                                           | Returns the cached value when `get` finds one. Otherwise runs `loader`, stores its result with `set` and returns it.                           |
| `delete(key)`                          | `Promise<void>`                                        | Deletes one key, or every key in an array.                                                                                                     |
| `flush()`                              | `Promise<void>`                                        | Deletes every key and typed entry of the current plugin. Other plugins' keys and unrelated data in the same Redis instance are left untouched. |
| `entry(definition, ...keyArgs)`        | `CacheEntryHandle`                                     | A typed entry. See [Typed entries](#typed-entries).                                                                                            |
| `acquireLock(key, ttlSeconds)`         | `Promise<boolean>`                                     | Takes a lock that expires after `ttlSeconds`. `true` when this call holds the lock, `false` when another caller does.                          |
| `releaseLock(key)`                     | `Promise<void>`                                        | Releases a lock taken with `acquireLock`.                                                                                                      |
| `status()`                             | `Promise<{ configured: boolean; connected: boolean }>` | Pings Redis. Both fields are `false` without Redis.                                                                                            |

`getSystem`, `getSystemMany`, `setSystem` and `deleteSystem` also exist. They write to a namespace shared with VitNode core, so plugins should use the plugin-scoped methods above.

## Keys

| Method                                             | Stored as                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `get`, `set`, `has`, `remember`, `delete`, `flush` | `vitnode:cache:{pluginId}:{key}`                                               |
| `acquireLock`, `releaseLock`                       | `vitnode:cache:__system__:lock:{key}`                                          |
| `entry(...)`                                       | `vitnode:cache-entry:{definition pluginId}:{name}:v{version}:{JSON key parts}` |

The plugin ID comes from the route that handles the request. Lock keys are not prefixed with it, so include your plugin ID in a lock key, for example `site-notes:rebuild-stats`.

## Serialization

Values go through `JSON.stringify` and `JSON.parse`:

- A `Date` comes back as an ISO string, and a `Map` or `Set` comes back as `{}`.
- `null` is stored, but `get` returns `null` for it, so `remember` treats it as a miss and runs the loader again.
- `undefined` is not stored.

## Typed entries

`defineCacheEntry` from your plugin's `@/api/builders` (`bindApiPlugin(manifest).defineCacheEntry`) declares an entry; `c.get("cache").entry(definition, ...keyArgs)` reads and writes it. A walkthrough is in [Typed cache entries](/docs/dev/cache/typed-entries).

| Name         | Type                                           | Required | Default    | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | `string`                                       | Yes      | -          | Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, up to 100 characters. Unique within the plugin. |
| `version`    | `number`                                       | Yes      | -          | Whole number, at least 1. Bump it to drop every stored entry. Never derived from the schema.    |
| `schema`     | `z.ZodType`                                    | Yes      | -          | Validates writes and reads. Its input must be JSON; `z.date()` is a compile error.              |
| `ttlSeconds` | `number`                                       | Yes      | -          | Whole number, at least 1. Capped at 15 by the in-memory fallback.                               |
| `key`        | `(...args) => (string \| number \| boolean)[]` | No       | `() => []` | Builds the key parts from `entry()`'s arguments. At most 8 parts: strings up to 256 characters, finite numbers or booleans. |

| Handle method      | Returns                        | Behavior                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get()`            | `Promise<Output \| undefined>` | The schema's output, or `undefined` on a miss. A stored `null`, `false`, `0` or `""` is a hit.                                      |
| `set(value)`       | `Promise<void>`                | Validates the schema's input and stores its JSON for `ttlSeconds`. Throws `CacheEntryValidationError` when invalid.                 |
| `remember(loader)` | `Promise<Output>`              | Returns the parsed hit, or runs `loader`, validates, stores and returns the parsed result. Throws like `set` for an invalid result. |
| `delete()`         | `Promise<void>`                | Removes the entry.                                                                                                                  |
| `key`              | `string`                       | The storage key, for logs.                                                                                                          |

- **Keys** belong to the plugin in the definition, not to the route handling the request. Key parts are encoded as a JSON array, so `"1"` and `1` are different keys and no part can collide with a string-API key.
- **Reads** treat malformed JSON, a value the schema rejects, a different `version`, no store and a Redis error as a miss; a rejected value is deleted.
- **Writes** copy the value to JSON first and reject a `Date`, `Map`, class instance, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `bigint`, circular reference, or `undefined` or missing (sparse) array item; `undefined` object properties are omitted. What is stored is that JSON (the schema's input), not the schema's output.
- **Errors:** `CacheEntryValidationError` for an invalid write; `CacheEntryDefinitionError` for an invalid `name`, `version`, `ttlSeconds` or key part. Redis errors are never thrown.

## Without Redis and when Redis fails

When the `redis` option in `vitnode.api.config.ts` is not set, the cache lives in the memory of each API process:

- It holds up to 10,000 keys and drops the least recently used one when full.
- Every TTL is capped at 15 seconds. A key written without a TTL stays until it is deleted or pushed out.
- `delete` and `flush` only reach the process that runs them. With one instance that is all of them; with several, the others keep their copy until it expires - hence the short cap.

Run more than one instance? Connect Redis so every instance shares one cache.

When Redis is configured but fails, the error never reaches your route. A failed read counts as a miss and a failed write is skipped. Commands fail immediately while Redis is unreachable instead of waiting in a queue, so an outage does not stall requests.

Locks behave differently, because a lock exists to stop work from running twice:

| Situation            | `acquireLock` returns |
| -------------------- | --------------------- |
| Redis connected      | `true` or `false`     |
| Redis not configured | `true` or `false`     |
| Redis error          | `false`               |

Without Redis, the lock only covers one process, and its TTL is not capped. If two instances must never run the same work at once, guard it in the database as well, for example with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.
